 By  
 Ryan O'Rourke 
 Published Oct 23, 2026, 8:30 PM EDT 
 Ryan O'Rourke is a Senior News Writer at Collider with a specific interest in all things adult animation, video game adaptations, and the work of Mike Flanagan . He is also an experienced baseball writer with over six years of articles between multiple outlets, most notably FanSided's CubbiesCrib . Whether it's taking in a baseball game, a new season of Futurama or Castlevania: Nocturne , or playing the latest From Software title, he is always finding ways to show his fandom. When it comes to gaming and anything that takes inspiration from it, he is deeply opinionated on what's going on. Outside of entertainment, he's a graduate of Eureka College with a Bachelor's in Communication where he honed his craft as a writer. Between The IV Leader at Illinois Valley Community College and The Pegasus at Eureka, he spent the majority of his college career publishing articles on everything from politics to campus happenings and, of course, entertainment for the student body. Those principles he learned covering the 2020 election, Palestine, and so much more are brought here to Collider, where he has gleefully written on everything from the SAG-AFTRA and WGA strikes to Nathan Lane baby-birding sewer boys.

 After a lengthy break from the screen, Christian Bale is officially booked and busy in Hollywood once more. The Oscar-winning star of American Psycho and The Dark Knight fame stepped away from the industry for a while after a red-hot 2022 that saw him join the MCU with Thor: Love and Thunder as the villainous Gorr the God Butcher , take center stage in the ambitious Amsterdam , and lead a chilling Netflix mystery in The Pale Blue Eye . Now, however, he's back with new releases and big plans on the horizon, including Prime Video's upcoming Madden biopic in November, in which he plays former Oakland Raiders owner, general manager, and coach Al Davis . He's also officially locked in to pick up where the legendary Al Pacino left off by playing Vincent Hanna in the much-anticipated Heat 2 .

 The real comeback for Bale, though, began much earlier this year with his turn in Maggie Gyllenhaal 's gothic monster romance, The Bride! . A wild reimagining of Bride of Frankenstein , the film casts the actor as the lonely Frankenstein's monster, who seeks the help of a scientist to make him a companion in 1930s Chicago. They find the perfect vessel in a woman murdered by the mafia and bring the titular Bride, played by Hamnet Oscar winner Jessie Buckley , to life. What follows is a madcap Bonnie and Clyde -like adventure, joining them on a spree of crime, romance, and liberation that becomes so much bigger than either could've imagined.
 The Bride! ultimately fell flat at the box office with just $24 million against a budget of over $90 million, but it has its fans for its gonzo style and blend of a wide range of genres, from period action to horror, romance, crime, and much more. Collider's Therese Lacson enjoyed the excess, saying in her 8/10 review of the film that " The Bride! embodies an unconventional and rebellious nature that makes it wholly unique." Those who want a more unconventional watch this Halloween now have another way to enjoy the divisive feature for themselves. Before Madden ever gets a snap on Prime Video, Gyllenhaal's monster movie has arrived on the streamer as of today.

 Collider Exclusive · 8 Questions · 2 Minutes 
 Which Iconic Romance Is Your Favorite? 
 Harry & Sally · Love & Basketball · Heated Rivalry · Titanic 
 Four great love stories, and four completely different ideas of what love actually is. One is a friendship that took twelve years to admit itself. One is two people who refuse to stop competing. One happens entirely behind closed doors. And one lasts five days and never stops mattering. Eight questions decide which one is really yours. 
 🍂 Harry & Sally (1989) 
 🏀 Love & Basketball (2000) 
 🏒 Heated Rivalry (HBO Max) 
 🚢 Titanic (1997) 
 FIND YOUR ROMANCE → 
 QUESTION 1 / 8 THE MEETING 
 01 
 How does your love story start? 
 The first scene tells you what kind of story this is going to be. 
 A We are friends for years before either of us says anything. 
 B We want the same thing and neither of us backs down. 
 C Nobody can know, including our closest friends. 
 D One look across a room and everything changes. 
 NEXT QUESTION → 
 QUESTION 2 / 8 THE FIGHT 
 02 
 What do the two of you keep arguing about? 
 Every great romance has one fight it has over and over. 
 A Whether this is actually happening, and what to call it. 
 B Whose career comes first this year. 
 C Whether we will ever be honest about this in public. 
 D Nothing small. When we fight, it is about everything. 
 NEXT QUESTION → 
 QUESTION 3 / 8 THE PROOF 
 03 
 How do you show somebody that you love them? 
 Grand gestures are easy to write. This is the harder question. 
 A I remember every single thing they have told me. 
 B I show up to the things that matter to them. 
 C I keep their secrets like they are my own. 
 D I would give up something enormous for them. 
 NEXT QUESTION → 
 QUESTION 4 / 8 THE OBSTACLE 
 04 
 What is actually standing in the way? 
 There is always something. Which something tells you the genre. 
 A Timing. We keep finding each other at the wrong moment. 
 B Ambition. We both want big lives and they do not match. 
 C The world. It is not safe to be open about this yet. 
 D Everybody around us has decided this cannot happen. 
 NEXT QUESTION → 
 QUESTION 5 / 8 THE MOMENT 
 05 
 Which romantic moment gets you every single time? 
 Be honest. There is one that works on you and you know which. 
 A Somebody running across a city to say it before midnight. 
 B Somebody in the stands who stayed until the very end. 
 C A look across a crowded room that nobody else catches. 
 D Somebody promising to hold on, and meaning it. 
 NEXT QUESTION → 
 QUESTION 6 / 8 THE RISK 
 06 
 What would you actually risk for the right person? 
 Every romance asks this. Most people find out far too late. 
 A A friendship I could never get back. 
 B The plan I have had for my life since I was a kid. 
 C My privacy. All of it would become public. 
 D Everything. I would not think about it for long. 
 NEXT QUESTION → 
 QUESTION 7 / 8 TEN YEARS ON 
 07 
 Where are the two of you in ten years? 
 Some love stories are about the meeting. Some are about the staying. 
 A Still talking. We have never run out of things to say. 
 B Building something together, both of us still ambitious. 
 C Finally open about it, after years of being careful. 
 D Apart, and I still think about it constantly. 
 NEXT QUESTION → 
 QUESTION 8 / 8 THE LINE 
 08 
 Which of these sounds most like something you would say? 
 Eight questions in, this is the one that decides your romance. 
 A I would rather talk to you than anybody else, forever. 
 B I am not giving up either of us. We find a way to have both. 
 C This is mine, and I am not explaining it to anyone. 
 D I would do the whole thing again, even knowing how it ends. 
 REVEAL MY ROMANCE → 
 Roll The Credits 
 Your Romance Is… 
 Four love stories, four completely different ideas of what it means to
 be somebody's person. This is the one that matches how you actually fall, and what it would ask of
 you.
 When Harry Met Sally · 1989 
 Harry & Sally 
 You do not fall for strangers. You fall for the person you have
 already been talking to for years, which is the slowest and by some distance the most
 durable way anybody has found to do this.
 When Harry Met Sally made the case that the best romance is an argument you enjoy,
 conducted over a decade, by two people refusing to admit what is happening.
 You want to be known rather than swept away. Somebody who remembers your worst story is
 doing better work than anybody arriving with flowers.
 The film is unusually honest about timing. These two are wrong for each other repeatedly
 until suddenly they are not, and neither of them engineered it.
 You would still be talking about everything at eighty. That is the entire promise.
 Love & Basketball · 2000 
 Love & Basketball 
 You want a partner, not an audience. Somebody who wants their own
 life as badly as you want yours, and who would never ask you to be smaller to make the
 relationship easier.
 This is the rare romance where both people have a real career and the film takes both of
 them equally seriously.
 You would rather be pushed than protected. The right person for you is also a bit of a
 rival, and that never entirely goes away.
 It understands the actual problem in ambitious relationships. Not whether you love each
 other, but whose turn it is this year.
 You would still be competing at forty. That is how you would know it was working.
 Heated Rivalry · Rachel Reid · HBO Max 2025 
 Heated Rivalry 
 The intensity was never the problem. The secrecy is. You are
 drawn to a love that lives entirely in private, and to the particular ache of wanting
 somebody you are not supposed to want.
 Heated Rivalry runs on the oldest engine in romance: two people on opposite sides,
 meeting in secret, getting far more attached than either of them planned.
 You keep your private life genuinely private, and something in you finds hidden things
 more real than public ones.
 The tension is not only between the two of them. It is between what they have and what
 it would cost either one to say it out loud.
 Years of this, and the whole story is really about whether either of them will finally
 stop hiding.
 Titanic · 1997 
 Titanic 
 You do not do this cautiously. When it happens for you it is
 immediate and total and it rearranges everything, and you would not accept a smaller version
 of it.
 Titanic gave us the biggest romance in film history and then made it last about five
 days, which is precisely the point of it.
 You measure love by intensity rather than duration. A few days of the real thing beats
 decades of something merely comfortable.
 The film is not only about the romance. It is about a woman who went on to live an
 enormous life afterwards because of it.
 You would still be telling this story at a hundred years old, and telling it exactly the
 same way.

 Who Else Is Involved in 'The Bride!'?
 Close Frankie and The Bride walk side by side down an alley. Image via Warner Bros. 
 The Bride is lying on an operating table with cables hooked to her heart. Image via Warner Bros. Discovery 
 The Bride is aiming a gun. Image via Warner Bros. 
 Frankie is shaking hands with Ronnie Reed. Image via Warner Bros. 
 In addition to directing, Gyllenhaal also penned The Bride! , also taking inspiration from Mary Shelley 's legendary Frankenstein in creating her distinct vision. This marked just her second feature behind the camera after previously helming 2021's The Lost Daughter . She also had a star-studded cast to work with beyond the two Academy Award-winning leads. Peter Sarsgaard, Annette Bening, Jake Gyllenhaal , Penélope Cruz , Zlatko Burić , and more are all on board for the ride.
 The Bride! is now available on Prime Video. Stay tuned here at Collider for more on all the hottest titles coming to and leaving streaming throughout the year.
